#263 round 1: PASS
Head: 2b0ce696554bd03a023193a584f916a904a160e9
Role: reviewer/263

No correctness findings within F213 / workstream 004 s08.

Lineage: registration.rs:720-803 returns only the daemon-observed ancestry after checking every pid/start tuple, the pane witness, and the current host again. The carry decision at 1193-1226 matches the stored stamped ProcIdentity against those ancestors, not a parent supplied in the registration claim. A reused pid or stale recorded start does not match; the same pane alone is insufficient. Ordinary reclaim has no native handoff, so cannot carry a proxied route.

Transitivity: any proxied stamp, including an earlier carried stamp, qualifies. Registration then stores the new host's proc, so another restart needs the immediately stamped process, not the original launch ancestor. The stamped ancestor must still exist in the verified parent chain with its original start time. A dead/reparented ancestor supplies no carry evidence; a disappearing process during observation fails verification. This is the intended conservative evidence rule, not ancestry reconstructed from stale pid values.

Behavior: every new lineage carry uses SeatCacheProxy::carried(), with the exact requested reason and no fix. Same-process registration and /new retain their existing route behavior. Explicit opt-out is retained for descendant and non-descendant replacements. Revive runs the spawn gate and writes a fresh proc-less descriptor with its own route (http/mod.rs:1551-1559,1664-1674); spawn binding preserves that new decision rather than carrying the old one.

Consumers: SeatSplit::of classifies by route state, so carried seats enter both the outage count and health.seats.proxied; justfile:97 prints that same doctor's list. The added carried-seat test exercises both classification and the outage notice. Workstream s08, blueprint 003 c-seat-proxy-state, their generated faces, API docs and the forward-only F221 note agree with the implementation.

Guard mutation review (read-only, not executed): changing the ancestor match to pid-only makes a_reused_pid_carries_no_route fail (same observed pid, stale stored start). Removing the descendant condition makes a_process_outside_the_stamped_lineage_reads_plain fail (same seat/session/pane, new host directly under SHELL instead of the stamped HOST). The positive test checks the exact carried reason, empty fix, and a carried stamp as the source for another carry. Tests enter register_native_with_observer and register_inner, rather than a duplicated decision helper.

Proof: just pr-freeze 263 returned FINAL at the full head above. CI run 44481004498 has that exact head and succeeded; rust-test job 135413038517 reports 2568 passed, 6 skipped. Its successful upload log identifies JUnit artifact 14508941087. Downloading that artifact by ID confirmed all six new regressions passed: a_restart_under_the_stamped_process_carries_its_route, a_reused_pid_carries_no_route, a_process_outside_the_stamped_lineage_reads_plain, an_opted_out_seat_stays_opted_out_across_a_restart, a_revived_launch_keeps_its_own_plain_stamp, a_carried_seat_counts_as_proxied. git diff --check origin/main...HEAD passed. No Cargo, shared-build, local Rust tests, or executed mutations.

Cost: no new loop, poll, timer, subprocess, environment read or token access. The existing bounded ancestry observation is retained, and the new match scans at most 31 ancestors only for a different launch. Existing macOS argv observation launches are unchanged; this PR adds zero launches and no recurring per-seat work. spawn_sites.rs is unchanged. Live before/after fleet cost receipts and post-deploy restart proof remain with their assigned performance/live-proof owners, not claimed by this correctness verdict.

Known limit: lineage is evidence of inherited launch configuration, not a reread of the effective route. A future Copilot that drops provider env on restart could be misclassified; s08 and D-F213-1 already state that residual. F221's already-lost stamps remain plain until revive, as ruled.

Local harness evidence limit: harness checks --quick exited 1 in this dependency-free review checkout: local tsx/vitest tooling is absent, typecheck cannot complete, and ambient Biome rejects the repository config. Native extension contracts, SDK contracts and the skill sensor passed; Rust, route-inventory and smoke were explicitly skipped. No dependencies were installed or symlinked, and the worktree remains clean. This is not a locally green ship gate.

Harness feedback / magicWand: a dependency-free review preflight that selects exact-head CI/JUnit receipts and reports unavailable local tools before attempting the developer gate would avoid repeating this known review-worktree friction. The request's suggested --role reviewer/263 syntax was refused as E-RS-ARG (a role id cannot contain a slash); the supported writer uses --role reviewer with --subject pr:263 and the request's --answers id. Encoding that distinction in the dispatch template would prevent the retry. No product or governance files were edited by hand.
